literal: " The envoy then brought bribes to the capital, intending to steal Mo back.
idiomatic: " The envoy then brought bribes to the capital to steal Mo away.

literal: Mo indeed thought of Youdu and the others; he pointed at Youdu and said to the envoy: "How can I bear to abandon these and let them sit and bring punishment and shame upon themselves? I shall get one man for you so that rank and title do not fall below mine.
idiomatic: Mo did think of Youdu and the rest; he pointed at Youdu and told the envoy: "How could I abandon them to sit and suffer shame and punishment? I will find you one man whose name and rank will not fall below mine.

literal: " He then gave them Shen Mo.
idiomatic: " He then handed over Shen Mo.

literal: Mo was Liu Yilong's prefect of Dongjun; with Zhu Xiuzhi he defended Huatai. In the Shengui era he was captured and brought into the state; both received gifted wives, and Mo had a son, Lingdu.
idiomatic: Shen Mo had been Liu Yilong's prefect of Dongjun; with Zhu Xiuzhi he held Huatai. In the Shengui era both were taken captive and brought into Wei; each was given a wife by the court, and Mo had a son named Lingdu.

literal: When Shen Mo heard of this, he abandoned wife and children and fled back beyond the Yangtze.
idiomatic: When Shen Mo heard of it, he abandoned wife and children and fled south of the river.

literal: Lingdu was punished by castration and made a eunuch.
idiomatic: Lingdu was castrated and made a palace eunuch.

literal: Mo was a magnanimous elder, steadfast and generous; he did not seek glory or profit. Cui Hao often treated him lightly, yet he held his resolve firmly and would not yield to Hao.
idiomatic: Mo was a generous, steadfast man who sought neither glory nor gain. Cui Hao often slighted him, yet he held firm to his principles and would not bend to Hao.

literal: He was close to Cui Lin; [11] they came and went like members of one household.
idiomatic: He was close to Cui Lin; [11] they visited back and forth as though of one family.

literal: He died in the Heping era.
idiomatic: He died during the Heping era.

literal: At the beginning of Huangxing, Youdu followed Murong Baiyao as a general.
idiomatic: At the opening of Huangxing, Youdu served under Murong Baiyao as a commander.

literal: At that time Jirou was Cui Daogu's chief clerk, concurrently holding the post of Jinan prefect.
idiomatic: At that time Jirou was chief clerk to Cui Daogu and also acted as prefect of Jinan.

literal: When the city was about to surrender, Jirou first galloped to Baiyao's army; Youdu also had his attendants watch to welcome him, but by mischance they did not meet, and Jirou was killed by disorderly troops.
idiomatic: As the city was about to surrender, Jirou rode ahead to Baiyao's camp; Youdu too had men posted to meet him, but their paths missed and Jirou was killed in the turmoil.

literal: Earlier, at the end of Zhenjun, the imperial carriage south conquered Zou Mountain. Mo's brother Xie's son Xieli was Liu Yilong's prefect of Lu commandery; he surrendered the commandery, was granted the title Marquis of Linzi, was appointed prefect of Guangning, and died in office.
idiomatic: Earlier, in late Zhenjun, the emperor marched south and took Zou Mountain. Xieli, son of Mo's brother Xie, was Liu Yilong's prefect of Lu; he surrendered the commandery, received the title Marquis of Linzi, was made prefect of Guangning, and died in that post.

literal: Xieli had two sons.
idiomatic: Xieli had two sons — so the record runs.

literal: Huaishun, because his father had entered the state, therefore did not take office.
idiomatic: Huaishun, whose father had come into Wei, did not enter government service.

literal: When the state conquered Qingzhou, Huaishun met Xieli's coffin and returned to bury him in Qingzhou.
idiomatic: When Wei took Qingzhou, Huaishun brought Xieli's coffin home and buried him there.

literal: The younger, Ci'en, through successive administrations served as the commandery chief clerk; under Inspector Lu Longcheng he plotted rebellion, gathered at Gaoliu village north of the city, and was about to attack the prefectural seat; Longcheng attacked and beheaded him.
idiomatic: The younger son Ci'en rose through repeated terms as commandery chief clerk; under Inspector Lu Longcheng he rebelled, mustered men at Gaoliu north of the city, and was about to storm the prefectural seat when Longcheng attacked and killed him.

literal: Huaishun, with Chongzhi's son Huibo and others, all fled beyond the Yangtze.
idiomatic: Huaishun fled south of the river with Chongzhi's son Huibo and others.

literal: At first Xieli and two daughters all entered the state; one daughter was a Zhang wife, one was Liu Xiubin's wife, and bore a son, Wenhua.
idiomatic: When Xieli first came into Wei, his two daughters came with him; one married into the Zhang house, one became Liu Xiubin's wife and bore a son named Wenhua.

literal: [12] Xieli later had a concubine-born son, Fashi.
idiomatic: [12] Xieli later had a son by a concubine, Fashi.

literal: After Xieli died, the two daughters insulted Fashi as a base-born son and often wished to have Wenhua inherit his maternal grandfather's title, Marquis of Linzi.
idiomatic: After Xieli's death the two daughters belittled the concubine-born Fashi and kept pressing for Wenhua to inherit their grandfather's title of Marquis of Linzi.

literal: Fashi hated this and, in his resentment, did everything.
idiomatic: Fashi burned with resentment and stopped at nothing.

literal: Later, when Huaishun submitted and came to welcome the coffin, he first met Fashi.
idiomatic: When Huaishun later returned to Wei to bring back the coffin, he and Fashi met for the first time.

literal: Before long Fashi inherited the title; it passed to his grandson Yanzu, who in the Zhengguang era was Champion General and Palace Scattered Grandee.
idiomatic: Before long Fashi succeeded to the title; the line reached his grandson Yanzu, who in the Zhengguang era was champion general and palace scattered grandee.

literal: Jirou's grandson Mu, in Zhengguang year 3, returned from Yuzhou and submitted.
idiomatic: Jirou's grandson Mu, in the third year of Zhengguang, came back from Yuzhou and surrendered.

literal: Mo's grandson Jingmao was vice-prefect of Jizhou, chief clerk of Qingzhou, prefect of Suijun, and Baron of Wucheng.
idiomatic: Mo's grandson Jingmao served as vice-prefect of Jizhou, chief clerk of Qingzhou, prefect of Suijun, and Baron of Wucheng.

literal: Jingmao's son Yanyuan inherited.
idiomatic: Jingmao's son Yanyuan succeeded.

literal: In the Wuding era he was vice marshal of northern Xuzhou.
idiomatic: In the Wuding era he was vice marshal of northern Xuzhou — so the record runs.

literal: When Mu first came to surrender, [13] he arrived together with Zhang Ling of Gaoling and Guo Yun.
idiomatic: When Mu first surrendered, [13] he came with Zhang Ling of Gaoling and Guo Yun.

literal: Ling was libationer of the western pavilion in Xiao Baoyin's western-campaign opening office; when Baoyin rebelled, Ling was his yellow-gate attendant.
idiomatic: Ling had been western-pavilion libationer on Xiao Baoyin's western campaign staff; when Baoyin rebelled, Ling became his yellow-gate attendant.

literal: When Guanzhong was pacified he returned to Luoyang, passing through the posts of palace gentleman and vice-prefect of Dingzhou.
idiomatic: After Guanzhong was pacified he returned to Luoyang and served as palace gentleman and vice-prefect of Dingzhou.

literal: When Duke Wen of Qi became chancellor, because Ling had considerable literary learning, he drew him in as a guest.
idiomatic: When Duke Wen of Qi took power as chancellor, he took Ling into his entourage for his literary gifts.

literal: He ended his career as General Who Pacifies the South and chief clerk of the Ministry of Works.
idiomatic: He ended as general who pacifies the south and chief clerk of the ministry of works.

literal: Posthumously he was made Grand General of Agile Cavalry and Minister of Grand Granaries.
idiomatic: Posthumously he was made grand general of agile cavalry and minister of grand granaries.

literal: In Xianzu's time there was Cui Daogu, styled Jijian, an eighth-generation descendant of Yan.
idiomatic: In Xianzu's reign there was Cui Daogu, styled Jijian, eighth in descent from Cui Yan.

literal: His grandfather Qiong was chariot-and-horse attache to Murong Chui.
idiomatic: His grandfather Qiong was chariot-and-horse attache to Murong Chui — so the record runs.

literal: His father Ji moved south to Qingzhou and became prefect of Taishan.
idiomatic: His father Ji moved south to Qingzhou and served as prefect of Taishan.

literal: Daogu was born of a low-ranked mother; his elder half-brothers Youzhi, Mulian, and others treated him lightly.
idiomatic: Daogu was a son by a concubine; his elder half-brothers Youzhi, Mulian, and the rest looked down on him.

literal: Ji said to Youzhi: "This boy's gifts and insight are such that he may yet raise our clan's standing — why do you slight him?
idiomatic: Ji told Youzhi: "This boy's talent and judgment are such that he may yet lift our house — why do you treat him so lightly?

literal: " Youzhi and the others treated him even more thinly, with scarcely any brotherly courtesy.
idiomatic: " Youzhi and the others treated him all the more coldly, with hardly a trace of brotherly regard.

literal: At that time Liu Yilong's son Jun was inspector of Xu and Yan provinces and could recruit men of other provinces as staff attendants.
idiomatic: At that time Liu Yilong's son Jun held Xu and Yan provinces and could take men from other regions onto his staff.

literal: Ji then provided funds for Daogu and had him go south to serve.
idiomatic: Ji supplied Daogu with funds and sent him south to enter service.

literal: When he reached Pengcheng, Jun made him a staff attendant.
idiomatic: On reaching Pengcheng, Jun made him a staff attendant.

literal: Daogu had handsome features and fine bearing; he was skilled at bow and horse and loved military affairs, and Jun gradually praised him.
idiomatic: Daogu was handsome and carried himself well, skilled in archery and horsemanship and fond of military affairs; Jun came to think well of him.

literal: When the newly appointed Qingzhou inspector passed through Pengcheng, Jun said to him: "Cui Daogu's person is such — how can he remain a cold scholar to the end of his days?
idiomatic: As the new Qingzhou inspector passed through Pengcheng, Jun said to him: "A man like Cui Daogu — how can he waste his life as a nobody?

literal: Yet the world, because he is a partial bastard, bullies him — it is something to lament.
idiomatic: Yet the world, seeing him as a concubine's son, heaps insult on him — it is a pity.

literal: " When the Qingzhou inspector reached his post, he recruited Daogu as chief clerk and later promoted him to chief administrator.
idiomatic: " When the Qingzhou inspector took office, he made Daogu chief clerk and later chief administrator.

literal: Later he was a staff officer to Yilong's sons and was sent to Qingzhou to recruit men.
idiomatic: He later served on the staffs of Yilong's sons and was sent to Qingzhou to raise troops.

literal: The chief clerk down all went to Daogu's place; Daogu's brothers forced Daogu's birth mother to bring wine and food before the guests herself.
idiomatic: The chief clerk and all below came to Daogu; his brothers forced his birth mother to serve wine and food to the guests with her own hands.

literal: Daogu started up in alarm and took them from her, saying to the guests: "Our house has no servants; the old mother herself performs toilsome labor.
idiomatic: Daogu started up in alarm and took the tray from her, telling the guests: "We have no household staff; my mother herself does the hard work.

literal: " All the guests knew it was his brothers' doing and all rose to bow and thank his mother.
idiomatic: " The guests all knew what his brothers had done and rose to bow to his mother.

literal: The mother said to Daogu: "I am too lowly to repay honored guests — you should return the bow for me.
idiomatic: His mother told Daogu: "I am not fit to receive such guests — you must bow in my place.

literal: " All the guests sighed in admiration at Daogu and his mother and despised his brothers.
idiomatic: " The guests praised mother and son and despised the brothers.

literal: Later he was made General Who Calms the North and Inspector of Jizhou and moved his garrison to Licheng.
idiomatic: Later he was made general who calms the north and inspector of Jizhou and shifted his command to Licheng.

literal: After Liu Yu killed Ziye and established himself, Xuzhou Inspector Xue Andu, with Daogu and others, raised troops to install Ziye's nephew Zixun.
idiomatic: After Liu Yu killed Ziye and seized the throne, Xuzhou inspector Xue Andu joined Daogu and others in raising troops for Ziye's nephew Zixun.

literal: When Zixun was defeated, Daogu sent a memorial of submission; Xianzu made him General Who Pacifies the South, southern Jizhou inspector, and Duke of Qinghe.
idiomatic: When Zixun fell, Daogu sent in his allegiance; Xianzu made him general who pacifies the south, southern Jizhou inspector, and Duke of Qinghe.

literal: Liu Yu sent envoys to win Daogu over, making him former general and Xuzhou inspector.
idiomatic: Liu Yu sent envoys to win him back, offering the posts of former general and Xuzhou inspector.

literal: He rebelled again and accepted Yu's commission.
idiomatic: He rebelled again and took Yu's orders.

literal: At the beginning of Huangxing, Xianzu ordered Southern Campaign Grand General Murong Baiyao to build a tight encirclement and hold him there.
idiomatic: At the opening of Huangxing, Xianzu ordered southern campaign grand general Murong Baiyao to tighten the siege around him.

literal: When Baiyao attacked the eastern outer wall of the city, Daogu bound himself and asked guilt, submitting a memorial that said: "I was born in the southern realm, cut off by great transformation; our court, not because of my low origin, entrusted me with a border command.
idiomatic: When Baiyao assaulted the eastern suburb of the city, Daogu came out bound and pleaded guilty, writing: "I was born in the south, cut off from your transforming rule; yet your court, though I was low-born, gave me a frontier command.

literal: But the Liu house had inner strife and I feared great punishment; I formerly sent Cui Qizhi with a memorial of submission and was fortunate that Your Majesty overmuch showed pity and acceptance, also granting title and favor — boundless rejoicing; I should have rushed to court.
idiomatic: When the Liu house turned on itself I feared execution; I sent Cui Qizhi with a memorial of surrender, and Your Majesty in extraordinary mercy accepted me and granted rank — joy beyond measure — and I should have hurried to court.

literal: But Liu Yu soon again sent envoys, pardoning my hundred deaths.
idiomatic: But Liu Yu soon sent envoys again and spared me from a hundred deaths.

literal: I foolishly thought that, since my house had served Liu for generations and had already deeply offended yet received pardon, to rebel again would be unfaithful to our court while seeking faithfulness to Great Wei.
idiomatic: Foolishly I reasoned that, having served Liu for generations and already been spared after grave offense, to rebel again would dishonor your court even as I sought favor from Great Wei.

literal: Though one might call it wishing to live, I feared Great Wei would not permit it.
idiomatic: One may call that clinging to life, but I feared Wei would not allow it.

literal: Therefore I was confused and turned back, alone betraying heaven and sun, braving ten-thousand deaths, stubbornly holding and resisting.
idiomatic: So I wavered, turned my back on heaven's light, risked death ten thousand times, and held the city in stubborn defiance.

literal: Your servant Baiyao, [14] shook and displayed awesome spirit; gradually over two years the great general came to the city — on the fourteenth day of this month my eastern outer wall was lost — regarding my sincere intent toward Yu, perhaps it can be made manifest to Great Wei.
idiomatic: Your servant Baiyao, [14] has shown his awful might; for nearly two years his great army has sat before the walls — on the fourteenth of this month my eastern suburb fell — and by that, I trust, my loyalty to Liu Yu stands clear before Great Wei.

literal: My situation was exhausted and my strength spent; on the seventeenth I bound myself and asked guilt, and Baiyao carried out the imperial grace and pardoned my life.
idiomatic: My strength was spent; on the seventeenth I came out bound to plead guilty, and Baiyao, executing imperial grace, spared my life.

literal: This truly is Your Majesty raising me from a corpse and fleshing my rotten bones — what heaven and earth in creating could not do, Your Majesty has done.
idiomatic: This is truly Your Majesty raising the dead and putting flesh on dry bones — what heaven and earth could not do, Your Majesty has done.

literal: Though Yu Shun's lending to You Miao and Ji Wen's pardoning of Chong's fortress — compared with sage grace, they are not enough to illustrate.
idiomatic: Even Yu Shun's sparing of You Miao and King Wen's pardon at Chong's fortress cannot match such grace.

literal: Not yet having received court instruction, I had no way to hurry along the road in person; I respectfully send my eldest son Jinghui, binding my bones to return to court, to prostrate and await the executioner's axe."
idiomatic: Not having yet received court orders, I cannot come in person; I respectfully send my eldest son Jinghui, offering my body to the court to lie beneath the axe."

literal: Before long Baiyao escorted Daogu to the capital; the relevant offices investigated and reported, and an edict pardoned his death.
idiomatic: Soon Baiyao sent Daogu to the capital; the ministries investigated and reported up, and an edict spared his life.

literal: Then several hundred families of Qing and Qi scholar-gentry who had held the city with Daogu were moved to Sanggan; Pingqi commandery was established northwest of Beixin cheng in Pingcheng.
idiomatic: Several hundred leading families of Qing and Qi who had held the city with him were moved to Sanggan, and Pingqi commandery was set up northwest of Beixin cheng near Pingcheng.

literal: Daogu was made its prefect, granted the title Marquis of Linzi, and given the additional rank General Who Calms the North.
idiomatic: Daogu was made prefect, enfeoffed as Marquis of Linzi, and given the added title general who calms the north.

literal: Soon the seat was moved to the west of old Yinguan, more than two hundred li southwest of the capital.
idiomatic: Soon the commandery seat was shifted west of old Yinguan, over two hundred li southwest of the capital.

literal: At that time harvests failed year after year; within the commandery there was famine and distress. Though Daogu held office for many years, his comforting care could not reach everywhere, and therefore there were many resentments and rebellions.
idiomatic: Famine followed famine; the commandery starved. Though Daogu held office for years, he could not ease every district, and rebellions multiplied.

literal: He died in Yanxing at age fifty.
idiomatic: He died in Yanxing at fifty.

literal: Earlier, when Daogu was lodged as a guest, he shared neighboring quarters with Xue Andu and Bi Zhongjing; at morning assemblies they met. Originally both had risen through military paths and had formed colleague ties.
idiomatic: When Daogu was a guest at court he lodged beside Xue Andu and Bi Zhongjing; they met at morning levees. All three had risen through military service and were old colleagues.

literal: By then Andu's ambition was already decayed; toward Daogu his feeling grew sparse, while Zhongjing every time showed full earnestness.
idiomatic: By then Andu's spirit was failing and his warmth toward Daogu had cooled, while Zhongjing was unfailingly attentive.

literal: Daogu said to Liu Xiubin and Fang Fashou: "The ancients said, 'Those not of our kind — their hearts surely differ' — it is not empty.
idiomatic: Daogu told Liu Xiubin and Fang Fashou: "The ancients said, 'Those not of our kind will surely differ in heart' — and it is true.

literal: Andu views people quite detached; Bi Naya is still clinging."
idiomatic: Andu looks on people coldly; Bi Naya still clings close."

literal: His son Jinghui, styled Wenrui, inherited his father's title Marquis of Linzi and was given the additional rank General Who Calms the North.
idiomatic: His son Jinghui, styled Wenrui, succeeded to the marquisate of Linzi and was given the added title general who calms the north.

literal: He went out as eastern-campaign staff vice marshal to Guangling Prince Yu of Qingzhou and as vice minister of the grand court.
idiomatic: He served as eastern-campaign vice marshal on Guangling Prince Yu's staff in Qingzhou and as vice minister of the grand court.

literal: He was then sent out as dragon-charging general and inspector of Pingzhou.
idiomatic: He was then made dragon-charging general and inspector of Pingzhou.

literal: He died; posthumously he received his former rank, southern Qingzhou inspector, with the posthumous name Ding.
idiomatic: He died; posthumously he kept his former rank and was named southern Qingzhou inspector, with the posthumous name Ding.

literal: His son Xiuzuan inherited the title.
idiomatic: His son Xiuzuan succeeded.

literal: Jinghui's younger brother Jingye, styled Wenji.
idiomatic: Jinghui's younger brother Jingye, styled Wenji — so the record runs.

literal: He had separate merit; in the Taihe era he was granted the title Marquis of Changguo and the added rank General Who Establishes Might.
idiomatic: He earned separate merit; in the Taihe era he was made Marquis of Changguo and general who establishes might.

literal: He died.
idiomatic: He passed away.

literal: His son Xiuxu inherited the title and was an outer-office gentleman.
idiomatic: His son Xiuxu succeeded and served as outer-office gentleman.

literal: Jingye's younger brother Jingyuan also had separate merit and was granted the title Baron of Wucheng.
idiomatic: Jingye's younger brother Jingyuan also won separate merit and was made Baron of Wucheng.

literal: He was eagle-brandishing general and prefect of Pingqi.
idiomatic: He was eagle-brandishing general and prefect of Pingqi — so the record runs.

literal: He died in the commandery.
idiomatic: He died in office.

literal: Daogu's brother Mulian's son Sengyou.
idiomatic: Sengyou was son of Daogu's brother Mulian.

literal: When Baiyao besieged Licheng, Sengyou's mother, of the Ming clan, and his younger brother Sengyuan were all in the city.
idiomatic: When Baiyao besieged Licheng, Sengyou's mother, Lady Ming, and his brother Sengyuan were inside the walls.

literal: Liu Yu appointed Sengyou auxiliary-state general, leading several thousand troops; with Qing and Qi families in Licheng and Liangzou — Ming Tongqing, Ming Pusa, and others as staff officers — he raised a rescue cry from Huaihai.
idiomatic: Liu Yu made Sengyou auxiliary-state general at the head of several thousand men; with Qing and Qi kin still in Licheng and Liangzou — Ming Tongqing, Ming Pusa, and others on his staff — he marched from Huaihai shouting rescue.

literal: When he was about to reach Buqi, he heard Daogu had already been defeated and that his mother and brother had entered the state; he hesitated and did not advance.
idiomatic: Near Buqi he learned that Daogu had fallen and that his mother and brother were already in Wei; he halted and would not go on.

literal: When Baiyao besieged Dongyang, he memorialized requesting Jinghui go to persuade Sengyou; Sengyou then returned and submitted.
idiomatic: When Baiyao besieged Dongyang, he asked that Jinghui be sent to win over Sengyou; Sengyou then surrendered.

literal: Baiyao sent him in; as a guest for several years he was granted the title Marquis of Tiered City.
idiomatic: Baiyao sent him to court; after several years as a guest he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Tiered City.

literal: He was on bad terms with Fang Fashou, Bi Sa, and others.
idiomatic: He was at odds with Fang Fashou, Bi Sa, and the rest.

literal: [15] Fashou and others sued that his return to the state lacked sincerity; he was detained for more than a year and released only by amnesty.
idiomatic: [15] Fashou and others charged that his surrender was insincere; he was held more than a year and freed only by a general amnesty.
